family.name: G-Class
family.verdict: A military box that became the world’s most expensive school-run accessory. Still devastating off-road — which most owners will never find out.
intro: The Geländewagen began as a military truck, commissioned in the early 1970s after the Shah of Iran — then one of Mercedes-Benz’s largest shareholders — pre-ordered some 20,000 of them. Mercedes engineered it; Steyr-Daimler-Puch built it in Graz, Austria, and production began in 1979.

The utilitarian [[g-class/w460|W460]] and later [[g-class/w461|W461]] served armies, border police and farmers. In 1990 the civilian [[g-class/w463|W463]] moved upmarket with full-time four-wheel drive and three locking differentials — and slowly turned into a luxury icon without ever losing its ladder frame.

For off-roaders, the sweet spot is the solid-axle W463 era, from the [[g-class/europa|Europa International]] imports of the 1990s through the [[g-class/g500|G 500]] and [[g-class/g550|G 550]]. The second-generation truck of 2018 is better on the road, with independent front suspension, and still carries three lockers.

page.title: G 500
page.verdict: A Cold War military design with leather, a V8 and three locking differentials. Lock all three at least once, if only to justify owning it.
page.hero_note: These are genuine 2002–08 G 500s, but on the street: we found no freely licensed off-road photo of this model year.

paragraphs: The G 500 is what happens when a military truck is asked to wear a suit and refuses to take its boots off. It was the first V8 G-Class built in regular production, the first one most Americans could buy from a Mercedes dealer, and — underneath the wood and leather — the same ladder-framed, triple-locked machine that armies bought by the thousand.

story.heading: A SHAH, AN ARMY AND A FACTORY IN GRAZ
paragraphs: The name goes back to Daimler-Benz’s six-wheeled G1 of 1926 — a Geländewagen, or cross-country vehicle — but the modern truck began in the early 1970s, when the Shah of Iran, then one of Mercedes-Benz’s largest shareholders, pre-ordered some 20,000 military vehicles. Mercedes engineered it; Austria’s Steyr-Daimler-Puch would build it in Graz. Design studies were carved in wood from 1973, and production began in 1979 — the same year the Shah fled Iran and his order evaporated.

It found other customers fast: border police, the Argentinian army and, in 1980, Pope John Paul II, who got one with a clear viewing platform. In 1983 a [[g-class/w460|280 GE]] driven by Jacky Ickx won the Paris–Dakar Rally, which settled any argument about whether it was a real off-roader.

story.heading: THE W463 GOES UPMARKET
paragraphs: In 1990 the civilian G was reworked as the [[g-class/w463|W463]]: a nicer cabin, full-time four-wheel drive and three fully locking differentials, while the utilitarian [[g-class/w460|W460]] and later [[g-class/w461|W461]] carried on separately. America still couldn’t buy one officially. New Mexico importer [[g-class/europa|Europa International]] converted European trucks to US spec — later persuading Mercedes to build them to DOT standards — and some sold for as much as $135,000.

The G 500 arrived in 1998 as the first regular-production V8 G — the hand-picked, limited-run [[g-class/500ge|500 GE]] of 1993 had come first — with the 5.0-litre M113, good for 292 hp. When Mercedes finally launched the G officially in the US for the 2002 model year, the G 500 and [[g-class/g55-amg|G 55 AMG]] were the two trucks in the showroom. The G 500 ran in America through 2008; for 2009 the same truck returned as the [[g-class/g550|G 550]] with a 5.5-litre V8 and a seven-speed automatic.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE EUROPA TRUCKS
callout.title: America’s G-Class before Mercedes sold one
paragraphs: Before 2002, the way to buy a new G in the US was Europa International of Santa Fe, New Mexico. Europa did the expensive work of federalizing European trucks, became the exclusive US importer with Small Volume Manufacturer status, and sold [[g-class/europa|300 GEs, G 320s and early G 500s]] with proper US VINs — 50-state legal, not gray-market. In 2002 Mercedes-Benz bought the US distribution rights and Europa turned to service, parts and the models America still never got, like the three-door Cabriolet.

A Europa G 500 looks like a 2002 truck from outside. Inside it’s simpler: a steering wheel and gauge cluster from the pre-facelift W210 E-Class (yes, the sedan), no factory radio controls on the wheel, and a 5-speed automatic without the later tip-shift gate. Enthusiasts like them for exactly that — fewer US-specific electronics to fail — and prices track 2002-on trucks.

page.engineering_intro: Strip the G 500 down and you find a 1970s off-roader that was never diluted. The body sits on a separate ladder frame. Both axles are solid, located by links and sprung on coils, so a twisted trail keeps the tires planted. Power goes through a two-speed transfer case to all four wheels all the time, and the three differential locks — centre, rear, front — let you turn it into something closer to a tractor when traction runs out.

engineering.note: Separate steel frame under the body — the reason Gs survive decades of abuse.
Coil-sprung and link-located. Independent front suspension only arrived with the 2018 redesign.
Two-speed transfer case with low range.
Three 100% locks, engaged from the dash.
292 hp, 456 Nm. Shared with the era’s E-, S- and ML-Class — parts are plentiful.
Approach and departure angles, per Hagerty. Track: 56 inches.

engineering_note.title: USING THE LOCKERS
engineering_note.body: Lock the centre first, then the rear, then the front — and only on loose surfaces at walking pace. Unlock in reverse once you’re through. On owners’ reports from mid-2000s trucks, the centre lock is vacuum-operated while the axle locks are hydraulic, which is why a single split vacuum fitting can take out the whole sequence (see repairs below).

buying_checks.head: Test all three locking differentials
buying_checks.body: Engage each lock on a loose surface and watch the indicators. Lockers that ‘were never used’ by the last owner often don’t work — budget for the vacuum diagnosis below.

buying_checks.head: Is it really an AMG?
buying_checks.body: Plenty of standard Gs have been dressed as AMGs. Check the VIN and data card against the badges before paying an AMG premium.

buying_checks.head: Listen at idle
buying_checks.body: Vibration or a chirp that changes with revs on an M113 points at the harmonic balancer — a known failure on early-2000s Mercedes V8s.

buying_checks.head: Look for oil on top of the engine
buying_checks.body: Wetness at the front of the V points at the oil filter housing seals; oil on the coil packs and exhaust manifolds points at valve cover gaskets or breather hoses. Neither is serious if fixed early, and both are reasonable DIY jobs (see repairs).

buying_checks.head: Look behind the front wheels
buying_checks.body: Gear oil on the inside of the wheels or the brake calipers means leaking front axle seals — and possibly contaminated brakes.

buying_checks.head: Drive it at 55–70 mph
buying_checks.body: Wander or steering shake at highway speed usually means a tired steering damper and worn linkage.

buying_checks.head: Rust where nobody cleans
buying_checks.body: Check the tailgate’s lower edge, door bottoms, sills, rear frame tubes, inner wheel arches and around the rear bumper.

buying_checks.head: A sagging headliner means water
buying_checks.body: Usually blocked sunroof drains. Water can reach the fuse box and climate actuators, so check those too.

repairs.title: Harmonic balancer (M113)
repairs.symptoms: Vibration at idle, a visibly wobbling crank pulley, rattle or chirp that changes with RPM, cracked or bulging rubber, belt squeal. Don’t keep driving it: if the outer ring lets go you lose power steering, charging and the water pump.
repairs.fix: Remove the belt and fan as needed, hold the crank with a counter-hold tool, and break the centre bolt loose. Fit the new balancer with a new centre bolt (it’s torque-to-yield) and a new front crank seal while you’re there. Torque to 200 Nm plus 90°.
repairs.tools: Crank counter-hold tool (MB 112 589 00 40 00 or equivalent) · 27 mm socket · long breaker bar or high-torque impact · new centre bolt (MB 112 031 00 71) · front crank seal · balancer (avoid used units with the failure-prone part numbers)

repairs.title: Oil filter housing gasket leak (M113)
repairs.cost: Parts cheap; most of the bill is labor
repairs.symptoms: Oil collecting at the top front of the engine in the V, running down the front of the block onto the belt, pulleys or harmonic balancer; a burning-oil smell once it reaches hot parts. Owners often get misdiagnosed first — on one M113 the first shop blamed the power steering pump.
repairs.fix: Confirm the source by degreasing the engine and checking again after a drive. Remove whatever sits over the housing (air intake ducting and covers), unbolt the housing, clean both mating faces completely and fit new seals. Use genuine Mercedes or Elring seals, torque to the factory figures, then degrease again so any remaining leak is easy to spot.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets and Torx/E-Torx bits · torque wrench · gasket scraper (plastic) and brake cleaner · new oil filter housing seals (genuine or Elring) · fresh oil and filter while you’re in there

parts.name: Reinz oil cooler / filter-housing gasket, lower (112 184 03 61)
Mann oil filter kit HU 718/5 x (000 180 26 09)

repairs.title: Valve cover gaskets & breather hoses (M113)
repairs.symptoms: Oil on the coil packs, plug leads and the top of the exhaust manifolds; a burning smell after a drive; in bad cases oil reaching the plugs and causing misfires. Breather hoses on the same engine family crack and leak too, so leaks around the covers aren’t always the gaskets.
repairs.fix: Remove the intake ducting, then the coil packs and plug leads (label them — the M113 runs two plugs per cylinder), then the cover bolts. Lift the covers, clean every trace of old gasket and sealant, and fit new gaskets plus the bolt grommets. Replace the crankcase breather hoses at the same time; where sealant is specified, owners report a continuous bead with no gaps and spotless surfaces is what stops repeat leaks. Torque the cover bolts evenly to the factory figure — overtightening distorts the covers.
repairs.tools: Sockets and Torx bits · torque wrench (low range) · plastic scraper and brake cleaner · valve cover gaskets and bolt grommets (genuine or Elring — owners report aftermarket gaskets leaking) · breather hoses · Mercedes-approved sealant where called for

parts.name: URO comprehensive M113 valve cover gasket kit

repairs.title: Diff locks won’t engage
repairs.symptoms: One or all locks refuse to engage, or engage then drop out; sometimes paired with central-locking oddities. The fault is usually the vacuum system, not the differentials.
repairs.fix: Confirm vacuum at the transfer-case hose. Then work from the pump and reservoir (front-left wheel well) through the manifold and the switchover valve block on the firewall, teeing in a gauge at each segment. One owner’s 2005 G 500 fault was a split plastic connector inside a rubber Y fitting under the brake booster. Change transfer-case and diff fluids and bleed the hydraulic locker lines while you’re in there.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump with gauge · assorted vacuum tees and line · replacement connectors · diff and transfer-case fluid · bleeding kit

repairs.title: Front axle seal leak
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inner front wheels, a gear-oil smell, oil on the caliper or rotor, brakes pulling to one side.
repairs.fix: Replace both front axle seals, not just the leaking side, and inspect the shafts for scoring. If oil has reached the brakes, replace the pads and resurface or replace the rotors.
repairs.tools: Axle seals (both sides) · seal driver · gear oil · brake pads and rotors if contaminated

parts.name: Genuine Mercedes front axle shaft seal 009 997 28 47
Liqui Moly 75W-90 synthetic hypoid gear oil (1 L)

repairs.title: Steering damper & front-end wander
repairs.symptoms: Highway wander, wheel shake around 55–70 mph, vague on-centre feel, clunks over bumps.
repairs.fix: Swap the steering damper (OEM or an upgraded unit such as a Bilstein B6). Check the drag link and tie-rod ends for play while you’re under there, then get an alignment.
repairs.tools: Steering damper · basic sockets and wrenches · tie-rod or drag-link ends if worn

repairs.title: Cracked coil springs
repairs.symptoms: A loud thump over bumps, uneven ride height, especially after cold weather.
repairs.fix: Replace springs in axle pairs. If you’re lifting the truck anyway, this is the moment to fit a lift spring kit (2-inch kits are common for the W463) with matched shocks.
repairs.tools: Springs (pairs) · jack and stands · spring compressor if required by your setup · new shocks recommended

parts.name: ARB/OME coil springs for 50 mm lift, W463

repairs.title: Sunroof drains & water ingress
repairs.symptoms: Damp or sagging headliner, wet carpets, electrical gremlins from a wet fuse box or climate actuators.
repairs.fix: Clear all four sunroof drains, then check the headliner, fuse box and blend-door actuators for water damage. Leaving it is what makes it expensive.
repairs.tools: Trimmer line or drain-cleaning wire · low-pressure air · towels and patience

parts.name: Mercedes sunroof drain hoses & connectors (search; match W463 part by VIN)

repairs.title: Propshaft judder
repairs.symptoms: Shake or judder under way, often worse under load.
repairs.fix: Inspect the joints and couplings for play before condemning the shaft. A worn shaft is a remove-and-replace job; mark the orientation so it goes back phased correctly.
repairs.tools: Sockets and wrenches · paint marker · replacement shaft or joints

parts.name: Mercedes driveshaft flex discs (search; match by VIN)

repairs.title: Rust on the frame and body
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling at the tailgate’s lower edge, door bottoms and sills; scale on the rear frame tubes and strut mounts.
repairs.fix: Catch it early: blast and treat, or weld in repair panels before it spreads. Cavity-wax the doors and underbody, rinse off road salt after winter, and keep drain holes clear. Severe frame rust can often be fixed in sections rather than with a whole new frame.
repairs.tools: Wire wheel or blaster · rust converter and primer · cavity wax · welder for panel repair

parts.name: Eastwood Internal Frame Coating (cavity wax for frame rails)
Eastwood Rust Encapsulator + Internal Frame Coating Plus kit

faq.q: What’s the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: A 275/70R18 — roughly a 33-inch tire — on the factory 18-inch wheels. Owners on Expedition Portal report it fits an unlifted G 500; one saw rubbing only on aftermarket ET63-offset wheels. A 285/65R18 can rub slightly at full left lock. Re-code the tire size with a Mercedes diagnostic tool so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

faq.q: What size are the factory tires?
faq.a: P265/60R18 on 18-inch wheels for 2002–2008 US G 500s — about 30.5 inches tall, which is why there’s room to go up.
7,000 lb with a braked trailer, across 2002–2008 G 500s. Unbraked limits are far lower — check your owner’s manual and local law.

faq.q: What kind of fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: EPA figures for a 2003: 11 mpg city, 13 highway, 12 combined, on premium fuel. Bigger tires, a roof rack and a lift make it worse.
Yes. The two-speed transfer case gives you low range for crawling, alongside full-time four-wheel drive.

faq.q: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
faq.a: No. Locked differentials stop the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and tires scrub. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed, and unlock before you’re back on tarmac.

faq.q: What’s the difference between a G 500 and a G 550?
faq.a: Mostly the engine and the badge. In the US the 2002–2008 G 500 has the 5.0-litre M113 V8; from 2009 the same W463 truck became the [[g-class/g550|G 550]] with the 5.5-litre M273 V8 and a seven-speed automatic.

faq.q: Will it fit in my garage?
faq.a: Plan on about 6.0 ft (1.84 m) tall for 2002–2003 trucks and 6.5 ft (1.98 m) for 2004–2008, with a 9.35 ft (2.85 m) wheelbase and roughly 15.5 ft of length. Add a roof rack and you’ll need to measure twice.

The frame, axles and V8 are tough; the age-related jobs are predictable — harmonic balancer, vacuum lines for the lockers, axle seals, steering damper, sunroof drains. A truck with records of these is a far safer buy than a low-mileage one that’s never been touched.

faq.q: How do I know if a G 500 is a real AMG?
faq.a: Check the VIN and the data card. Many standard Gs wear AMG bumpers, wheels and badges, so the badges alone tell you nothing.

mods.why: Complete travel-ready builds: lift, armor, racks, lighting and storage, done as one coherent truck.
Sympathetic restorations of older Gs for owners who want factory-correct, not flashy.
Lift springs and upgraded shocks to clear bigger all-terrains and carry weight.
Flat platform racks and rear ladders for tents, recovery gear and spares.
Kits that bring 4×4²-style capability and stance to a standard G.
Smaller wheels with taller all-terrain sidewalls — the single most transformative change.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing was done and reset every fluid and filter in the first month: on a 15–25-year-old G 500 the expensive failures (722.6 shifts, diff locks, front axle seals) usually trace back to old fluid, perished vacuum lines or a skipped knuckle service. Read the tags on the transfer case and axles before buying fluid — W463 drivetrains changed through the years.

items.spec: MB 229.5 · 0W-40 or 5W-40 full synthetic · ≈8.0 L (8.5 qt) with filter
items.interval: Then yearly or at the service indicator
items.note: Cartridge filter in a housing on top of the engine — use a 74 mm, 14-flute cap wrench. While it's open, look for weeping at the filter-housing gaskets.

parts.name: Liqui Moly 5W-40 oil change kit, 8 L + filter (G 500 2002–08)
Mann oil filter kit HU 718/5 x (000 180 26 09)

items.interval: Now, then with every second oil change or sooner on dirt roads
items.note: Check the airbox for leaves and rodent nests on a truck that sat.
A clogged filter on a G is often wet too — check for sunroof-drain water while you're in there.

items.note: Oil in the plug wells means valve-cover gaskets — fix those first, then fit plugs, wires and any oil-soaked coil boots.

items.note: Drop the pan, fit a new filter and gasket, and replace the 13-pin connector sleeve — ATF wicking through it ruins harnesses. Set the level hot, on level ground, with the 722.6 dipstick tool.

items.note: Fill plug on the front right, drain plug underneath with a small magnet; both are 14 mm hex. Inspect the propshaft flex discs (in pairs) and the centre support bearing while you're under it.
